source_headline: Someone tagged a fancy Pacific Heights co-op tower. Even neighbors are kind of impressed
angle_statement: The crew that rappelled down a Pacific Heights tower is based in Taiwan, which makes this graffiti tourism rather than a local statement.
tldr: Two writers from the Taiwan-based EO4 crew rappelled down an art deco co-op on Vallejo Street and painted three-story pieces. They signed them San Fran.
editor_note: The crew that rappelled down a Pacific Heights tower is based in Taiwan, which makes this graffiti tourism rather than a local statement. One piece near the roof reads we own ur city now. The writers do not live here, have done the same in Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Thailand, and the Philippines, and gave themselves away by writing San Fran, which is a thing no one from here says. That detail changes what the piece is. Pacific Heights read it as a security failure and a bill, since a co-op pays for its own removal to avoid city fines. Neighbors read it as craft. Both responses assume a conversation with San Francisco that was never actually happening.
what_to_watch: The co-op has to paint over the pieces at its own cost to avoid city fines, and no arrests have been reported.

fail_reasons: check_1_recap: the source runs 542 words and the note delivers most of its substance (who painted it, the Taiwan crew, the rooftop text, the country list, the co-op paying for removal, the split neighbor reaction). A reader who reads only the note has the whole story and no reason to click through. The graffiti-tourism read is genuinely ours. Suggested fix: build the note on the San Fran signature and what it implies, and drop the neighbor reactions and the removal-cost detail entirely.
